novelty.justification: The claim proposes a new phenomenon/mechanistic relationship—“reasoning models allocate progressively less self-verification effort to later steps” while “late steps are exactly where an injected error is most likely to corrupt the final answer”—rather than merely applying a method to a new object; its proposed measurement is a decaying, steerable “verification-engagement” residual-stream signal. Searches using “verification recency gradient,” “within-chain verification effort,” “late-stage fragility chain-of-thought,” “self-verification positional bias,” and “residual stream verification steering” found the closest related works in Self-Verification Dilemma: Experience-Driven Suppression of Overused Checking in LLM Reasoning (2026), Self-Correction Bench (2025), and the cited ASCoT late-error-fragility work; these address overused checking, activation of self-correction, or positional error consequences, but not the claimed anti-alignment between spontaneous checking and fragility. The step from those works to this claim requires a new core relationship—positional verification allocation as the mechanistic cause of late fragility—although the proposed linear probing, activation patching, and steering are standard tools, so this is high within the existing framework rather than paradigm-level novelty.
